rfi.description: The Plan International charity said Monday that global warming has increased the risk of child marriages, teenage pregnancies and violence against girls. Its report coincides with talks in the South Pacific nations of Fiji and Tuvalu, where climate change is affecting all aspects of daily life.

rfi.title: Study shows extreme poverty, homelessness on the rise in France
rfi.description: An international study published Monday by France’s largest food aid charity Restos du Cœur shows that the number of people living in extreme poverty in France and other wealthy countries, increased by 37 percent between 2018 and 2025.

rfi.title: Chat group kingpin goes on trial in Paris over online abuse of underage girls
rfi.description: A 29-year-old man went on trial on Monday at the Paris Assize Court, charged with running a masculinist chat group on the platform Discord on which young victims were forced to engage in sexual acts online and to mutilate themselves.

rfi.title: Spain PM calls early election after housing crisis defeat
rfi.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday called a snap election for 29 November, after parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government. This comes after tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities on Saturday to demand affordable housing.

rfi.title: US-German trio win medicine Nobel for work on optogenetics
rfi.description: The Nobel medicine prize was awarded Monday to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their work in the field of optogenetics.

rfi.title: Nobel Prize announcements begin, with hopes of a 'less controversial year'
rfi.description: With this year's Nobel Prize winner announcements beginning on Monday, among those experts believe could be in line for the $1.2 million prizes are GLP-1 researchers, a Ukrainian children's rights activist and several female authors. And after last year's Donald Trump-driven controversy, anticipation around this year's Peace Prize is high.

rfi.title: The pill: from symbol of women's liberation to subject of growing mistrust
rfi.description: Initially a symbol of liberation, the pill went on to become an almost inevitable part of a woman’s contraceptive journey. But today its use in France is in decline, the drop in popularity fuelled by health warnings, mistrust and a changing attitude towards contraception.

rfi.title: Ethiopia captures Tigray capital as its regional rivals meet in Egypt
rfi.description: Ethiopian federal forces have regained control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, local sources said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

rfi.title: France struggles to fund farm climate adaptation as losses mount
rfi.description: Farmers in France are expecting their first payments shortly under the government's billion-euro emergency aid package to support farmers affected by severe summer heatwaves, droughts and wildfires. As the effects of climate change worsen, experts say compensation alone will not be enough to protect French agriculture in the long term.

rfi.title: Rwandan genocide hunter Dafroza Gauthier dies after long battle for justice
rfi.description: Dafroza Gauthier, who spent spent decades tracking down Rwandans in France accused of involvement in the 1994 genocide, has died from cancer at the age of 72. By filing a string of civil lawsuits against suspected fugitives, she and her husband Alain pushed the French legal system to hold them to account.

rfi.title: Reintroduction of vultures to France causes friction with farmers
rfi.description: France’s vulture population is growing, thanks to a reintroduction campaign that began in the 1980s after the birds all but disappeared decades earlier. But according to some farmers, the return of the birds has brought challenges as well as rewards.

rfi.title: Cry for help as French-Swiss lake dries up in record summer heat

lemonde.title: Schneider Electric, fabricant de prises devenu un géant de l’électrification, fait une acquisition majeure aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: La multinationale a annoncé lundi 5 octobre le rachat de l’éditeur de logiciels américain PTC sur la base d’une valorisation de 20,1 milliards d’euros, le plus important rachat de son histoire mouvementée. La Bourse n’a pas apprécié.

france24fr.title: Ligue des nations : la France renverse la Belgique dans un festival offensif
france24fr.description: Menée à la pause, l’équipe de France a renversé la Belgique en 15 minutes pour s’imposer (4-1). Grâce à cette victoire, les Bleus sont premiers du groupe 1 après quatre matches.

france24fr.title: En Russie, Moscou visée par une des attaques les plus massives contre la capitale
france24fr.description: Les autorités russes ont indiqué, mardi, que Moscou a été la cible d'une attaque de 650 drones dans la nuit, faisant deux morts et neuf blessés, dans la périphérie de la capitale. La plupart des appareils "ont été détruits par la défense antiaérienne" a fait savoir le maire de la capitale.

france24fr.title: Mouvement lycéen: "Comment stopper l'escalade ?"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, l’inquiétude, en France, avant «l’acte III», aujourd’hui, de la mobilisation des lycéens. Un mouvement critiqué pour ses débordements, tandis que plusieurs voix s’élèvent contre les «violences policières» dont il serait la cible. L’annonce, hier, en Espagne, de législatives anticipées le 29 novembre prochain. Et le vingtième anniversaire, demain, de l’assassinat de la journaliste russe Anna Politkovskaïa, le 7 octobre 2006.

france24fr.title: Au-delà de la mobilisation lycéenne, une bataille du récit entre LFI et le gouvernement
france24fr.description: Critiquée par le gouvernement sur son rôle dans le mouvement des lycéens et dans les débordements des derniers jours, La France insoumise répond avec un contre-récit sur les violences policières. Jean-Luc Mélenchon entend faire de la protection de la jeunesse l’élément central de la journée de mobilisation du 6 octobre.

france24fr.title: En direct : mobilisation massive attendue des lycéens en France pour l"'acte III"
france24fr.description: Mardi, la mobilisation des lycéens, qui signe l'"acte III" du mouvement, s'annonce massive. Des syndicats ont d'ores et déjà indiqué se joindre à la contestation. Hier, des centaines d'établissements étaient fermés et un jeune de 15 ans a été gravement blessé. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Au Québec, les indépendantistes de retour au pouvoir avec un référendum en ligne de mire
france24fr.description: Le Parti québécois de Paul St-Pierre Plamondon a remporté, lundi soir, les élections au Québec, avec environ 28 % des voix mais sans majorité absolue, compliquant la mise en œuvre de son programme. Le nouveau Premier ministre de cette province canadienne a précisé qu'il attendrait la fin du mandat de Donald Trump pour organiser un référendum sur l'indépendance.

france24fr.title: Trump permet désormais à tous les Américains d’acheter du diesel détaxé
france24fr.description: Le président américain, Donald Trump, dont la cote de popularité souffre des prix à la pompe, a signé, lundi, un décret visant à autoriser tous les Américains à acheter du "diesel rouge exonéré de taxes". Le texte se limite en réalité à reporter le paiement de la taxe sur ce gazole normalement réservé aux machines agricoles.

france24fr.title: Fusillade de Fort Hood en 2009 : le tireur sera exécuté par peloton
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a donné, lundi, son accord pour que Nidal Malik Hasan, un ancien psychiatre de l'armée américaine qui avait tué 13 personnes sur la base texane de Fort Hood en 2009 pour protester contre les guerres en Afghanistan et en Irak, soit mis à mort par peloton d'exécution.

france24fr.title: "Acte III" : nouvelle journée de mobilisation lycéenne sous haute tension en France
france24fr.description: Des dizaines de milliers de lycéens manifestent sous haute surveillance, mardi, à travers la France pour réclamer des moyens, un "Acte III" soutenu par une intersyndicale de l'Éducation nationale. Plus de 6 000 interpellations ont été effectuées depuis le 28 septembre.

france24fr.title: UE : ces villes où le loyer dévore les salaires
france24fr.description: Selon la Commission européenne, les prix de l'immobilier ont augmenté de 60% depuis 2013. Ce mardi, les députés européens ont donc décidé de débattre des moyens de rendre le logement plus abordable d'autant que les 27 sont loin d'être égaux dans ce domaine. Les villes les plus chères ne sont pas forcément celles où la pression du logement est la plus élevée.

france24fr.title: Les Houthis du Yémen disent avoir frappé l'aéroport de Riyad, en Arabie saoudite
france24fr.description: Les Houthis ont revendiqué, lundi, des frappes contre l'aéroport international de Riyad, une raffinerie du pétrolier Aramco et des sites du sud de l'Arabie saoudite. Activant leur pacte de défense mutuelle, la Turquie et le Pakistan annoncent l'envoi de militaires dans le royaume. De leur côté, les forces yéménites lancent une contre-offensive sur Sanaa.

france24fr.title: Les exportations de pétrole brut revenues à leur niveau d'avant-guerre
france24fr.description: La circulation des navires pétroliers a partiellement repris dans le détroit d'Ormuz et la péninsule arabique a réorganisé ses flux de pétrole, via l'oléoduc saoudien est-ouest ou celui vers Fujairah, sur le golfe d'Oman. Mais les tensions persistent sur les produits raffinés. Et si les membres du G7 ont accepté de libérer 100 millions de barils de leurs réserves stratégiques, la Chine, elle, recommence à acheter du pétrole pour reconstituer ses stocks.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : pluies torrentielles dans plusieurs villes, de lourds dégâts
france24fr.description: Plusieurs grandes villes du Sénégal ont enregistré des pluies torrentielles ce dimanche. C'est le cas de Kaolack, Matam mais aussi Dakar et sa banlieue. Des personnes ont trouvé la mort dans les inondations selon le chef de l’Etat sénégalais. Le bilan est encore imprécis. Le gouvernement dit avoir activé un plan d’urgence et des mesures d’assistance aux sinistrés. Reportage de nos correspondants à Dakar Simon Martin et Elimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Ligue des nations : la France renverse puis punit la Belgique
Ligue des nations : la France renverse puis punit la Belgique grâce au coaching de Zidane
france24fr.description: Les Bleus ont remporté lundi leur duel face à la Belgique au Stade de France en Ligue des nations. D'abord menés par la Belgique contre le cours du jeu, les Français ont fait la différence en fin de match grâce à l'entrée des remplaçants Cherki, Olise et Doué (4-1).

france24fr.title: "La France tombe" : l'extrême-droite anglosaxonne instrumentalise les violences en France
france24fr.description: Les blocages de lycées se poursuivent en France et avec eux, les violences. L'extrême droite anglosaxonne les commente et les instrumentalise quitte à ce que des fausses informations soient relayées.

france24fr.title: Brésil : Lula peut-il encore gagner ?
france24fr.description: Au Brésil, c’est une surprise : Flavio Bolsonaro, ultraconservateur et fils de l’ex-président Jair Bolsonaro, est sorti en tête du premier tour de la présidentielle ce dimanche, avec 47 % des voix contre 45 % pour le président sortant Lula. Le sénateur de 45 ans et le président sortant de 80 ans s’affronteront le 25 octobre pour le second tour. Dans un pays ultrapolarisé, chacun espère récupérer les abstentionnistes et les reports de voix.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : plus de 140 000 inscrits à la primaire de la gauche
france24fr.description: Pour voter les 9 et 10 octobre à la primaire de la gauche sociale-démocrate, plus de 140 000 personnes se sont inscrites, a annoncé, dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, la commission organisatrice. Lors des trois débats, les échanges houleux entre Glucksmann et Faure sur une éventuelle alliance avec LFI ont éclipsé les sujets de fond.

zeit.title: Bevölkerungsentwicklung: So zukunftsfähig ist Ihre Region
zeit.description: Neue Daten zeigen, wie sich Deutschland demografisch und wirtschaftlich entwickelt. Alter, Kinder, Bildung: Was die Prognosen bis 2045 über Ihren Landkreis verraten.

zeit.title: Gaza: Israel versetzt Armee vor 7. Oktober in Alarmbereitschaft
zeit.description: Die israelische Regierung will Geheimdienstinformationen zu möglichen neuen Hamas-Angriffen haben. Verteidigungsminister Katz droht den Menschen in Gaza. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Bahn: Güterzug mit Gegenstand kollidiert - Ausfälle im Nahverkehr
Russland: Russland spielt Berichte über Pestfall in Sibirien herunter
zeit.description: In Sibirien stirbt eine Mitarbeiterin eines Pestforschungsinstituts. Die russische Führung weist den Verdacht, dass sie sich mit der Pest infiziert haben soll, von sich.

zeit.title: Radaraufnahmen vom Feind: Panzerbauer Rheinmetall erschließt Weltall als Geschäftsfeld
Fußball: Nach Karriereende: Ex-Herthaner Demme spielt Icon League
Konstituierung des Landtags: Landtagsamt und Generalsekretär? Für Siegmund kein Problem
Verbraucherberatung: Fünf neue Angebote: Der Beratungsbedarf der Thüringer steigt
Notfälle: Großeinsatz an Schule im Kreis Verden
Regionalliga: Pokal-Schreck Jeddeloh II trennt sich von Trainer
Tobias Rausch: »Ich bin kein Hardliner«
zeit.description: Er stand im Zentrum der Vetternwirtschaftsaffäre, heute soll er erster AfD-Landtagspräsident werden. Respekt vor dem hohen Amt? Tobias Rausch hat seine eigene Sichtweise.

zeit.title: Ukrainekarte aktuell: Ukraine erobert Gelände in Region Charkiw zurück
zeit.description: Die ukrainische Armee meldet die Einnahme von rund zehn Quadratkilometern nahe der Grenze zu Russland. Russische Truppen infiltrieren Dobropillja.

zeit.title: Jeffrey Archer: Britischer Schriftsteller Jeffrey Archer mit 86 Jahren gestorben
zeit.description: Der Autor vieler Bestseller und ehemalige britische Politiker Jeffrey Archer ist tot. Erst vor Kurzem signierte er noch Bücher und sollte seinen neuen Roman vorstellen.

zeit.title: US-Bomber in Großbritannien: US-Bomber wegen möglichen Drohnenangriffs von Stützpunkt abgezogen
zeit.description: Die Sorge vor einem Drohnenangriff führte offenbar zum überraschenden US-Abzug von einem Stützpunkt in England. Militärkreise gehen von einem iranischen Komplott aus.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN WIRTSCHAFT - Die Arbeitslosenquote verharrt im September bei drei Prozent
BILDSTRECKE - Die Schülerproteste in Frankreich dauern an – die Bilder der Eskalation
nzz.description: Die Schüler- und Studentenproteste in Frankreich haben sich zu einer landesweiten und zunehmend gewaltsamen Massenbewegung entwickelt. Für heute Dienstag wurde zu einem nationalen Aktionstag und zu Grossdemonstrationen in Städten wie Paris, Lyon und Marseille aufgerufen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Cristiano Ronaldo erkennt nicht, wann es Zeit ist zu gehen, und beschädigt damit sein Renommee
nzz.description: Mit 41 Jahren steht Ronaldos Karriere vor dem Ende, doch der portugiesische Fussballstar sucht die richtige Form des Rücktritts. Sein ewiger Konkurrent Lionel Messi handelt klüger.

nzz.title: Ein letzter Besuch in Delhi: Parmelin zieht vor seinem Abtritt in Indien Bilanz seiner Handelspolitik
nzz.description: Die Aussenhandelspolitik hat seine Amtszeit im Departement für Wirtschaft geprägt. Einer seiner grössten Erfolge war das Abkommen mit Indien. Vor seinem Rückzug aus dem Bundesrat sieht Parmelin die Schweiz gut gerüstet für die Zukunft.

nzz.title: Der Bundesrat und das Säuli: das ungeschriebene Protokoll der Olma
nzz.description: Am 8. Oktober wird Bundespräsident Guy Parmelin in St. Gallen die Olma eröffnen und mit einem Ferkel in den Händen für die Fotografen posieren. Woher stammt die Tradition des bundesrätlichen Säuli-Fotos?

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Bei der AfD kennen die Kirchen keine Gnade
nzz.description: Immer wieder müssen Kirchenmitarbeiter gehen, weil sie für die AfD kandidieren. Mit dieser kalten Selbstgewissheit schaden die Kirchen sich selbst.

nzz.title: Rechter Asyl- und linker Wirtschaftsminister? SVP heizt Spekulationen über Departementsverteilung an
nzz.description: Beat Jans könnte als erster Sozialdemokrat ins Wirtschaftsdepartement wechseln, die SVP liebäugelt mit dem EJPD. Doch wie gross wäre der politische Spielraum der neuen Chefs wirklich? Und könnte der Bundesrat eine Rochade verhindern?

nzz.title: Der Bundesrat will die Kantone zum Frühfranzösisch zwingen. Doch diese lassen sich das nicht gefallen
nzz.description: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider will per Gesetz erreichen, dass bereits in der Primarschule eine Fremdsprache gelernt wird. Der Widerstand dagegen ist enorm – auch FDP und SVP wehren sich gegen das Sprachdiktat.

nzz.title: «Ich schätze, ich bin einfach ein heimlicher Nazi . . .», sagt der Star-Podcaster Tucker Carlson und verheddert sich in Aussagen um Grossbritanniens Rolle im Zweiten Weltkrieg
nzz.description: Ist das Vereinigte Königreich 1939 «freiwillig» in den Krieg eingetreten? Der Star-Podcaster Tucker Carlson duelliert sich mit dem früheren Tory-Minister Rees-Mogg und zeigt ein bizarres Geschichtsbild.

nzz.title: Neue Erkenntnisse zum Flydubai-Flug: Co-Pilot soll Tat schon vor seiner Anstellung geplant haben
nzz.description: Nach dem versuchten Anschlag eines Co-Piloten werden neue Details zu Ziel und Planung bekannt. Warnsignale gab es offenbar schon Jahre zuvor.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Putin hat eine neue Strategie: Sie beruht allein auf Kriegsverbrechen
nzz.description: Russlands Terror gegen die Ukraine hat eine neue Stufe erreicht. Das Ziel besteht offensichtlich darin, Städte wie Kiew unbewohnbar zu machen. In dieser Situation braucht die Ukraine für ihre Verteidigung mehr denn je westliche Hilfe.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Auch nach zwei Todesspritzen lebt Christa Pike noch – wie kann das sein? Das Wichtigste zum misslungenen Hinrichtungsversuch in den USA
nzz.description: Die zum Tode verurteilte Mörderin hätte schmerzfrei sterben sollen – stattdessen wird sie nun im Spital beatmet. Wie Fachleute sich die gescheiterte Exekution erklären.

nzz.title: Frankreich ermittelt gegen mutmassliche Hamas-Finanzierer
nzz.description: Zwei französische Hilfswerke sollen Gelder an die Hamas weitergeleitet haben. Ihre Leiter stehen im Verdacht, die Terrororganisation mit Kryptowährungen finanziert zu haben.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Frankreich könnte zum Zentrum einer neuen Euro-Krise werden. Das Misstrauen der Anleger steigt und steigt
nzz.description: Die Rendite französischer Staatsanleihen ist auf dem höchsten Stand seit 2002. Das Land hat keine Kraft für dringende Reformen. Dennoch sollte die EZB unbedingt von einer Intervention absehen.

nzz.title: In diesem Herbst ist die Nations League mehr als bloss lästige Pflicht. Und die Schweizer Fussballer beweisen ihre Seriosität
nzz.description: Mit einem weiteren Sieg gegen Nordmazedonien könnte das Nationalteam bereits am Dienstag den Aufstieg in die Liga A schaffen. Dan Ndoye wird für die Schweiz immer wertvoller – er steht für die Hartnäckigkeit von Yakins Ensemble.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Teure Treibstoffe: «Ich bin 38 Jahre in dieser Branche. So eine Lage wie derzeit habe ich noch nicht erlebt.»
nzz.description: In Cressier im Kanton Neuenburg steht die einzige Raffinerie der Schweiz. Sie hat 60 Jahre überlebt – und läuft jetzt auf Hochtouren. Ein Gespräch mit Konzernchef Dev Sanyal über die Abhängigkeit Europas.

observador.title: Morreu Luís Torres, dono do Elefante Branco
observador.description: Em prisão preventiva desde julho de 2025, o empresário dono do clube noturno lisboeta Elefante Branco morreu vítima de cancro do pulmão em estado avançado.

observador.title: "Uma “deusa” no 25 de Abril" e turismo de saúde em Portugal
observador.description: O novo episódio de "Os Escândalos de uma Revolucionária". Os médicos alertam que o turismo de saúde em Portugal está "fora de controlo" e o primeiro-ministro discursa esta manhã no Parlamento Europeu.

observador.title: Morreu aos 86 anos o escritor e ex-político Jeffrey Archer
observador.description: O autor conhecido por livros como "Quem não Arrisca..." ou "Escondidos à Vista de Todos" morreu esta segunda-feira. Informação foi divulgada pela editora HarperCollins.

observador.title: Cirurgião admitido na UMinho pede apoio para sair de Gaza
observador.description: Cirurgião ortopédico na Faixa de Gaza foi admitido no mestrado de Biomedicina na Universidade do Minho em maio. Instituição de ensino apelou à diplomacia portuguesa para que possa sair de Gaza.

observador.title: E, agora, um breve interlúdio de poesia e lugares-comuns
observador.description: André Ventura (que quer começar já a CPI a Luís Neves), José Luís Carneiro (que não quer mudar nada nas rendas) e o Presidente (que fez um discurso inconsequente) são o Bom, o Mau e o Vilão.

observador.title: Trump apelou a Macau para intervir em litígio sobre nome
observador.description: Disputa teve origem quando Trump tentou obter os direitos exclusivos sobre a marca "Trump" no território, numa altura em que manifestava interesse em expandir os seus negócios para Macau.

observador.title: Dois em cada três jovens europeus sofreram abusos
observador.description: Estudo foi realizado a 26 mil pessoas entre os 18 e os 30 anos, na UE, Noruega e Islândia. Um em cada cinco inquiridos revelou ter vivido quatro ou mais tipos de experiências adversas na infância.

observador.title: Brasil: e agora?
observador.description: A contagem decrescente para a segunda volta já começou. Para lá da disputa entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula da Silva, as peças do xadrez movem-se: como se enfrentam os EUA e a China nestas eleições?

observador.title: A Vinted tornou-se num pesadelo até para quem pede 2 euros?
observador.description: Vender na Vinted é sinónimo de exigir medidas milimétricas por uma pechincha de dois euros. A baixa de Lisboa virou réplica para turistas com latas de sardinha do Cristiano Ronaldo a preços de ouro.

observador.title: Bolsas de nicotina vão quarta-feira ao parlamento
observador.description: Em causa está a discussão da proposta de lei que autoriza o Governo a aprovar o regime jurídico aplicável ao fabrico, distribuição, comercialização, rotulagem e publicidade das bolsas de nicotina.

observador.title: A32 cortada no sentido Norte-Sul após despiste de camião
observador.description: Alerta para o acidente foi dado às 6h46 e às 7h30 estavam no local sete operacionais e cinco viaturas. Ferido de veículo pesado foi assistido no local.

observador.title: 8h. PM tenta evitar cortes nos fundos comunitários
observador.description: Luís Montenegro discursa em Estrasburgo quando os Estados-membros e o Parlamento Europeu negoceiam o próximo orçamento comunitário. Ainda, Governo reúne-se com sindicatos da Função Pública.

observador.title: Medvedev perde a cabeça e acerta em cheio num adepto?
observador.description: De Medvedev a ser corrido de Pequim por acertar num fã aos portugueses que sonham com o Golden Boy, sem esquecer a piada da praxe com o nome de João Félix.

observador.title: Vale a pena arriscar 600 mil euros para partilhar jornais?
observador.description: O grupo Impresa pede uma pesada indemnização a dois homens por piratearem jornais na internet. Pelo meio, Carl Becker avisa que a comunidade precisa de funerais para salvar a saúde da comunidade.

observador.title: Trump retira impostos a gasóleo vermelho
observador.description: Gasóleo destinado a utilizações fora da estrada, como a agricultura, está isento de impostos especiais. Viagem de Trump ao Nebraska fez parte de maratona de comícios de 32 dias.

observador.title: Pedro Sánchez vai sobreviver ao poker das eleições?
observador.description: Cercado por casos de corrupção, o primeiro-ministro espanhol joga a cartada eleitoral. E ainda, a ressurreição do bolsonarismo, o turismo de saúde no SNS e o apelo de Seguro que PS e PSD vão ignorar.

observador.title: Técnicos dos serviços prisionais em greve
observador.description: Sindicato mantém a sua "discordância relativamente ao valor do suplemento de risco", que considerou insuficiente face às responsabilidades, exigências e riscos inerentes ao exercício das funções.

observador.title: Europa está desprotegida contra a guerra híbrida?
observador.description: Miguel Baumgartner alerta para a incapacidade europeia em responder às operações de sabotagem russa. Considera também que Trump tenta isolar a Polónia para pressionar os restantes aliados.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Neuer Infraplan soll Entwicklung des Schienennetzes steuern
spiegel.description: Mit dem sogenannten Infraplan will der Bund klare Vorgaben für das Schienennetz machen. Kann die Bahn so wieder flott werden? Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: USA: Weißes Haus verweigert »Politico« Zutritt zur »Air Force One«
spiegel.description: Vor Gericht wehren sich mehrere US-Medien gegen ihren Ausschluss aus dem Weißen Haus. Nun darf »Politico« auch nicht mehr in die Präsidentenmaschine. Berichterstattung von dort sei ein »Privileg«, so eine Trump-Sprecherin.

spiegel.title: Coco Gauff siegt in Peking: US-Tennisstar beklagt rassistische Kommentare im Netz nach Match
spiegel.description: Weil die LED-Anzeigen in der Arena sie irritierten, beschwerte sich Coco Gauff, erhielt recht – und gewann das Match in Peking. Ihre erst 16 Jahre alte Gegnerin war den Tränen nahe. Danach schlug Gauff im Netz der Hass entgegen.

spiegel.title: »Lebensgefährliche Mängel« – Warentest und ADAC warnen vor zwei Autokindersitzen
spiegel.description: Beim Crashtest brachen wichtige Komponenten der Kindersitze, stellten ADAC und Stiftung Warentest fest. Hersteller Britax Römer kündigt eine Untersuchung an, Axkid leitet einen Rückruf ein.

spiegel.title: Boris Palmer setzt lieber auf Talkshows als auf ein Ministeramt
spiegel.description: Als Talkshowgast bewirke er mehr als in jedem Ministerium, findet der Ex-Grüne Boris Palmer, der mit etlichen Skandalen von sich reden machte. Warum er kein Minister ist, hat Palmer zufolge drei Gründe.

spiegel.title: In Siegen stinkt es – und keiner weiß warum
spiegel.description: Über der Innenstadt von Siegen liegt ein metallischer, brandähnlicher Geruch. Feuerwehr und Umweltamt suchen nach der Ursache – bislang vergeblich, ähnlich wie vor 14 Tagen.

spiegel.title: USA: Prominenter Parteifreund von Donald Trump bereut Unterstützung für Hegseth
spiegel.description: Seine Stimme hätte den Unterschied machen können. In einem Buch bereut der Republikaner Thom Tillis nun, dass er dennoch für Pete Hegseth stimmte. Auch zu Gesundheitsminister Kennedy hat er eine klare Meinung.

spiegel.title: Michael Olise führt Frankreich gegen Belgien mit Gala-Auftritt zum Sieg
spiegel.description: Sieben Tore hat Frankreich unter Zinédine Zidane bislang erzielt. An sechs davon war Michael Olise beteiligt. Gegen Belgien überragte der Angreifer des FC Bayern, danach gab es ein Sonderlob vom Trainer.

spiegel.title: Gemeinde Südharz: Im Harz brennen 1000 Strohballen - Ende der Löscharbeiten nicht absehbar
spiegel.description: Rund 1000 Strohballen stehen in der Gemeinde Südharz in Flammen. Die Feuerwehr kämpft gegen den Brand. Wegen der starken Rauchentwicklung gab die Rettungsleitstelle eine Warnmeldung heraus.

spiegel.title: Elektromobilität: Verkehrsbetriebe fahren größtenteils Verbrennerbusse
spiegel.description: Der Umstieg auf Elektromobilität geht in den Großstädten nur äußerst schleppend voran, zeigt eine neue Untersuchung. In einigen Städten sind sogar überhaupt keine Elektrobusse im Einsatz.

spiegel.title: Fedor Holz: Ex-Pokerstar zeigt seinen Kalender und spricht über Entschleunigung
spiegel.description: Fedor Holz war 2016 der erfolgreichste Pokerspieler der Welt, erspielte Millionen an Preisgeldern. Bei seiner jetzigen Arbeit im Finanzwesen setzt er auf Entschleunigung. Und hat kein Problem damit, Termine abzubrechen.

spiegel.title: Amazon Prime und Prime Day: Ist Amazons Abodienst noch sein Geld wert?
spiegel.description: Regulär kostet Amazon Prime 90 Euro pro Jahr. Über ihr Abo bezahlen viele Mitglieder Dinge mit, die sie gar nicht kennen oder nutzen – wie Cloudgames, einen Fotospeicher und alte Fernsehzeitschriften.

spiegel.title: Schweden: 18-Jähriger stirbt bei Busunglück - Dutzende Verletzte

phys-org.title: California scientist wins a Nobel Prize, then makes school lunches for his kids
phys-org.description: Dr. Karl Deisseroth spent hours fielding congratulatory calls after learning early Monday that he had won a Nobel Prize for medicine for helping to open a new field of brain science called optogenetics.

phys-org.title: Switching on brain cells: The Nobel-winning science of optogenetics
phys-org.description: In optogenetics, scientists control neurons by stimulating them with light—potentially unlocking breakthroughs for conditions such as dementia, depression and blindness.

phys-org.title: Russia reports a worker at a Siberian plague institute got pneumonia from an unknown cause and died
phys-org.description: Russian authorities have quarantined a hospital and are monitoring contacts of an employee at a plague research institute in Siberia who contracted pneumonia of an "unknown" cause. Local state TV said the woman died last week.

phys-org.title: Carefree shoppers most likely to receive retail discounts, study finds
phys-org.description: Research involving Durham University Business School reveals how retailers target customers most likely to spend more. Shoppers who take a more carefree approach to spending are more likely to receive personalized discount codes from retailers, according to the research.

phys-org.title: Exploring systemic racism as the default explanation for disparities
phys-org.description: Much of the field of sociology treats systemic racism as its default explanation for racial disparities rather than as an open question that requires further investigation and evidence, according to a recent position paper. The assumptions and moralization surrounding the origins of race-based disparities have undermined the discipline and made it difficult—and professionally costly—to challenge the concept, says author Ilana Redstone, a professor of sociology at the University of Illinois Urban

phys-org.title: Vitamin B1 gains in wild lake trout embryos challenge assumptions drawn from hatcheries
phys-org.description: For decades, fisheries managers have struggled to restore recruitment in wild lake trout populations across the Great Lakes region, with limited success. Returning this species to its former abundance is hampered by overfishing, sea lamprey predation, invasive species and habitat alterations.

phys-org.title: Global review reveals major blind spots in our understanding of climate change impacts on Mediterranean ecosystems
phys-org.description: A new global review of observed climate change impacts on plant communities reveals major gaps in where and how we monitor some of the world's most climate-vulnerable ecosystems.

phys-org.title: Neutrons, rotating black holes, and a galactic PeVatron at the center of the Milky Way
phys-org.description: Galactic black holes are cosmic mitochondria, powerhouses of the universe. Most of the energy these supermassive black holes produce comes from the material surrounding them: superheated plasma in their accretion disks interacting with tremendous magnetic fields. But there is a more direct way to extract energy from a black hole. It's known as the Penrose process, and a new study asks whether we could discover a signature of this process.

phys-org.title: Why some Indigenous communities don't resist oil extraction in their territories
phys-org.description: More than half of the Ecuadorian Amazon has been marked for oil drilling, overlapping with Indigenous territories and areas of high biodiversity. The ecological and cultural impacts of oil extraction are well documented and have fueled some of Latin America's most prominent environmental movements. Yet at the local level, extraction is not always met with resistance.

phys-org.title: Global soil erosion outpaces natural recovery, report warns
phys-org.description: Isaac Larsen, an associate professor in the College of Natural Sciences' Department of Earth, Geographic, and Climate Sciences, is a lead author of "Status of the World's Soil Resources 2026," a new report produced by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) that draws on recent scientific literature and contributions from hundreds of experts around the world.

phys-org.title: Political orientation and institutional trust emerge as key factors in local wind energy support
phys-org.description: Why does the expansion of wind energy sometimes meet with local resistance, even though renewable energy generally enjoys broad support? RIFS researcher Jörg Radtke used a representative survey of 6,284 people in North Rhine-Westphalia to investigate which social characteristics are linked to the acceptance of wind energy.

phys-org.title: Game simulator shows how math can guide decisions when resources are limited
phys-org.description: In "Bloons Tower Defense," the goal is to stop balloons from reaching the end of a track by strategically placing towers along the route. These towers vary in cost, range and attack power, and they also take up valuable space. The game becomes increasingly difficult with each round. Where you place a tower therefore determines not only how effective it is now but also which options remain available later in the game.

phys-org.title: 'Digital ibuprofen' offers Chinese youth comfort through cute characters facing familiar struggles
phys-org.description: In China, young people are encountering a myriad of challenges, from societal pressures around success to life in a highly surveilled society, that have led them to turn to the internet in search of a balm to soothe their pain. What has emerged is a host of content called "digital ibuprofen"—viewed as a way to numb the anxieties of modern living.

phys-org.title: Attention can't be bought, so brands turn to memes
phys-org.description: The funniest post you saw this week may not have come from a friend; it may have come from a brand. Whether it is Kohl's, Wendy's, or Netflix, brands are behaving more like internet users than traditional advertisers.

phys-org.title: Unusual senses: The secret superpowers of amphibians and reptiles
phys-org.description: The Surinam toad is one of the strangest frogs on Earth. Flat-bodied, tiny-eyed and adapted to the murky waters of the Amazon basin, it hunts well despite having very poor vision. When a fish swims close, the frog suddenly opens its mouth and sucks the prey inside in a fraction of a second.

phys-org.title: What a locust can teach us about how neuromodulators alter odor processing
phys-org.description: When you walk into a bakery and smell fresh cookies, the enticing smell draws you in. After you eat a handful of cookies, though, the same smell likely doesn't send you back for more. Researchers in the McKelvey School of Engineering at Washington University in St. Louis sought to determine the biological mechanisms in the brain that controllably alters odor-evoked behavior by using an unlikely model—a locust.

phys-org.title: Rhinos and elephants can cause huge problems if reintroduced badly—here's how to get it right
phys-org.description: Moving large animals around is a seductive idea in conservation. If there are plenty of animals in one place and too few in another, moving some between the two seems an obvious solution. Sometimes it is. But with animals as large, mobile and socially complicated as elephants and rhinos, the move itself can turn out to be the straightforward part.

phys-org.title: Quantum interactions may have locked early universe's fields into existing energy states
phys-org.description: The universe may be trapped in its own comfort zone, and a researcher in the College of Engineering and Computer Science has helped explain why it cannot seem to leave. A new study suggests the universe could be locked into its current state by the same kinds of quantum effects that scientists study when trying to preserve fragile information inside a quantum computer.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
proj-syn.description: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

proj-syn.title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
proj-syn.description: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia's usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

proj-syn.title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
proj-syn.description: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

proj-syn.title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
proj-syn.description: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

proj-syn.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
proj-syn.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

proj-syn.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
proj-syn.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

proj-syn.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
proj-syn.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

proj-syn.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

proj-syn.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
proj-syn.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

proj-syn.title: The Hard Road to a Middle-Power Order
proj-syn.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. Yet they are increasingly turning to coalitions of the willing and a patchwork of separate initiatives that risk entrenching zero-sum mindsets and making collective action harder.

proj-syn.title: The Sovereign Wealth Fund America Needs
proj-syn.description: Two recent proposals to establish a new US sovereign wealth fund would fail to make good on a good idea, because neither plan would produce a fund nearly large enough to meet America’s mounting financing needs. But a different approach, funded by Treasury sales, could.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.
